axes.runtime:
**Cross-platform Wasm apps on the WasmEdge runtime** — "cross-platform portable Wasm app that can run on many
CPU and GPU devices" (README); install WasmEdge first, then download a GGUF + a .wasm app and run.
GitHub LlamaEdge/LlamaEdge Apache-2.0 1,663 stars, pushes stopped 2026-02-08 (API verified);
the latest release 0.29.0 was published the same day (2026-02-08).
axes.local_files: Reads and writes local files — GGUF model files, .wasm app files; wasmedge --dir .:. mounts the current directory.
axes.background:
A CLI/local-service process (OpenAI-compatible web endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings,
/v1/audio/transcriptions, etc. — README endpoint list); no persistent cloud surface.
axes.tools: The OpenAI-compatible API endpoint surface + the CLI chat app; not an agent-tool host.
axes.context:
No cross-session memory (it is an inference-serving surface) — context length follows the GGUF model and WasmEdge preload parameters;
conversation state is carried by the client, the server stores no sessions.
axes.permissions: Runs locally; the permission surface = local files and CPU/GPU. The Wasm sandbox is the runtime layer's selling point (WasmEdge wording).
axes.fit:
Fits: the WASM portability route — one .wasm app across many CPU/GPU devices; edge/embedded scenarios (the WasmEdge ecosystem).
Does not fit: an active release cadence (main-repo pushes stopped 2026-02-08); llama.cpp's full native feature surface (the WASM layer is a transpiled route).

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/runner/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/runner/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- Whether there is any migration/successor statement after the update pause (most repos in the org stopped updating from 2025; no official statement found)
- The support matrix of each GPU backend (CUDA/Metal) on the WasmEdge side (docs pages exist; not verified item by item)
- The release repos and version cadence of each of the six model lines (README category links point to different repos)
related: Backend contrast: LlamaEdge compiles llama.cpp-lineage inference into Wasm running on WasmEdge; GGUF is the same source.
Contrast: Ollama is a productized wrapper; LlamaEdge is the portable-Wasm route, aimed at edge devices.
Same family: both are OpenAI-compatible local serving stacks; LocalAI goes the Go backend-plugin route, LlamaEdge the Wasm-app route.

Consumer-side contrast: coding agents like Aider can point at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — once LlamaEdge serves a local endpoint, agent workflows can run on the WASM inference stack (endpoint compatibility is where the two lines meet).
